scope: Non-model calls of the n8n content pipeline only. OpenRouter model calls are not priced here: their cost is reported by OpenRouter, or estimated from the model price when the node drops usage (see INVENTORY.md section 1).
rule: unit_price_usd null means the price is unknown: the collector writes cost_usd NULL and counts the call in unpriced_calls. Never 0 unless the call is known to be free.

brightdata.web_scraper_api.basis: Pay-as-you-go list price, $1.50 per 1,000 records, billed for successful records only.
brightdata.web_scraper_api.count_units_from: Number of records delivered: the scrape response itself when it returns records, otherwise BrightData Scrape2 / Get BrightData Reddit Snapshot(/Retry). Progress and snapshot polls are not billed separately.
brightdata.web_scraper_api.source: brightdata.com/pricing/web-scraper-api as quoted by search results, and dupple.com/pricing/bright-data (dated October 2026). brightdata.com itself is blocked by the Xsolla VPN, so the official page was not opened.
brightdata.web_scraper_api.open_question: Which BrightData plan is the account on? On the $499/month Scale plan the rate is $1.30 per 1,000 after 384,000 included records, and dataset-specific rates can differ.

nodes.HTTP Request2: zone web_unlocker1, POST api.brightdata.com/request, sites other than Reddit/Facebook/Telegram/VK

brightdata.web_unlocker.basis: Pay-as-you-go list price, $1.50 per 1,000 successful requests; failed requests are not charged.
brightdata.web_unlocker.count_units_from: 1 per execution of HTTP Request2 whose response is a page, 0 when it errored (node has continueRegularOutput, so check the output for an error).
brightdata.web_unlocker.source: brightdata.com/pricing/web-unlocker as quoted by search results. Official page blocked by the Xsolla VPN.
brightdata.web_unlocker.open_question: Same as above: plan and actual rate for zone web_unlocker1.

nodes.Compress Video: POST /ffmpeg/process (only when Needs Compression? is true)

ffmpeg_service.ffmpeg_api_com.basis: Monthly subscription metered in GB-seconds = (input GB + output GB) x processing seconds; only successful operations that produce output count. Published plans: Starter $11/month for 500 GB-s, Pro $39/month for 2,000 GB-s, Growth $99/month for 5,000 GB-s. No per-call or overage price is published.
ffmpeg_service.ffmpeg_api_com.count_units_from: Unknown. The docs do not say whether the API response reports GB-seconds per call, or whether /directory, /file and /ffprobe/analyze use quota.
ffmpeg_service.ffmpeg_api_com.open_question: Which plan is the account on? Should the ledger spread the monthly fee over GB-seconds (about $0.02 per GB-s on any plan), or record these calls as unpriced? Does a response carry the GB-seconds used?

koka.telegram_parser.basis: Unknown. Looks like a partner or internal service.
koka.telegram_parser.open_question: Does telegram-parser.koka.team charge per call, a flat fee, or nothing? If nothing, set unit_price_usd to 0.
